description: The plot illustrates the training loss over time for two models: “Vanilla” and “SepLLM,” as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis represents training time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds with major tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis shows the loss value on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks every 0.05 units. The “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with triangular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 2.75 loss at 0 seconds and gradually decreases to about 2.62 by 250,000 seconds. The “SepLLM” model is shown with a red line and circular markers, also solid, starting near 2.73 and declining to approximately 2.61 by 250,000 seconds. A green dashed line, labeled “1.26×,” is drawn from the point where SepLLM reaches a loss of ~2.60 at around 180,000 seconds to the corresponding point on the Vanilla curve at ~225,000 seconds, visually indicating that SepLLM achieves the same loss level 1.26 times faster than the Vanilla model. Both curves exhibit a steep initial decline followed by a slower convergence toward a plateau.
